status: estimated-average-demand; hardware protection and assembly remain unqualified

cell.name: One XTAR protected INR21700-50E 5000 mAh button-top

mapping: Clamp each shared Godot RGB channel times electrical brightness to [0,1], round to the nearest 8-bit PWM code; no optical gamma, shader brightness, reflections or glow. A modeling scenario, not a delivered firmware cap.

operating_basis.excluded_normal_use: Full-white, full-brightness operation is outside the intended use. It is not the runtime sizing case.
operating_basis.led_model: Adafruit NeoPixel engineering estimate: 20 mA per fully driven RGB channel plus a separately retained 1 mA logic allowance per powered pixel.
operating_basis.pattern_model: Sample the shared Godot RGB functions over the full eight-second cycle. The full-saturation HSV rainbow has mean R+G+B of 1.5 before 8-bit quantization, so its dynamic channel demand averages half of RGB white at equal brightness.
operating_basis.brightness: 5% is the calculator default, not a firmware-enforced ceiling. Other brightness settings require their own demand calculation.
operating_basis.protection: Use average estimates for runtime and normal operating load planning. Retain separate inrush, fault, cutoff, recovery and thermal checks; software brightness is not a hardware fault limit.

evidence.claim: Selected protected button-top INR21700-50E: 3.6 V nominal, 5000 mAh nominal, overcharge/over-discharge/short protection. Nominal 18 Wh is not guaranteed usable energy or a qualified recovery/thermal/fault bound.

Adafruit uses 60 mA RGB white and a rough 20 mA per pixel animation budget. The active model resolves the actual RGB channels; it does not multiply that animation budget by another one-third rainbow factor. Equal 20 mA channel coefficients are the adopted planning approximation.

Adafruit describes primary-color current as about one-third of white and its saturated rainbow average duty near 50%. Our actual HSV RGB samples, rather than a fixed rainbow discount, determine demand.
Adafruit uses about 1 mA logic current per powered dark pixel. The active model retains this allowance at zero brightness and under moving dark masks; it does not scale idle current with brightness.
Measured two WS2812B products at approximately 33.5 and 52.5 mA maximum and just under 1 mA dark. These are sensitivity evidence for variation, not measurements of our Fibonacci board.

Reference comparison only: 16/11/15 mA red/green/blue plus 1 mA dark at 5 V. These measured-strip calibration coefficients are not substituted into the selected Adafruit model, and FastLED hsv2rgb_rainbow is not our Godot HSV function.
Regulator minimum input is 2.9 V; typical no-load quiescent current below 1 mA is not a maximum efficiency or quiescent bound.
The NeoPixel planning approximation also applies to the current ring counts. Exact strip stock, protection and assembly ratings remain separate design work.

uncertainty: Estimated NeoPixel average demand from Adafruit channel/idle figures and the actual shared RGB pattern. Pixel variants differ; PJRC measurements show this variation. Controller/radio load, efficiency, path loss and reserve remain adjustable planning assumptions. Calculated runtime is an estimate, not a measured result. Sampled frame peaks exclude internal PWM, radio bursts, inrush and faults; hardware protection and thermal qualification remain separate.
